_about: Integrity note labels and explanations as the student reads them on the result page (GAD-T606), keyed by the note's type. The English is IntegrityExplanations' own wording, word for word (LocalizationTests checks); reviewer pages keep reading IntegrityExplanations, and English results use it directly. A type with no key here shows IntegrityExplanations' English.
integrityNote.looked-away.label: Looked away
integrityNote.looked-away.explanation: Ordinary. Looking away has many causes (recalling, planning an answer, nerves, a noise, a habit, reading something), and the camera cannot tell which. On its own it is not a sign of dishonesty.
integrityNote.gaze-away.label: Looked away
integrityNote.gaze-away.explanation: Ordinary. Looking away has many causes (recalling, planning an answer, nerves, a noise, a habit, reading something), and the camera cannot tell which. On its own it is not a sign of dishonesty.
integrityNote.glance.label: Glanced away
integrityNote.glance.explanation: Normal. Brief glances away from the screen happen in every conversation and mean nothing on their own.
integrityNote.face-absent.label: No face in view
integrityNote.face-absent.explanation: The camera did not see a face for this stretch. Often harmless (the student leaned out of frame, adjusted the camera, or the lighting changed); check whether answers continued during it.
integrityNote.multiple-faces.label: More than one face
integrityNote.multiple-faces.explanation: The camera saw a second face. Could be someone helping, or someone simply walking past; look at whether the answers around this time changed.
integrityNote.identity-drift.label: Possibly a different person
integrityNote.identity-drift.explanation: The face partway through did not closely match the one at the start. Camera angle and lighting cause false alarms; compare with the start of the session.
integrityNote.offscreen-reading.label: Reading pattern off-screen
integrityNote.offscreen-reading.explanat: A sustained look at one off-screen spot with repeated left-to-right sweeps, which can be reading notes or another screen. Webcam eye tracking is too coarse to tell reading from other eye movement reliably, so this is a guess from the movement, not a finding; check it against the answers given.
integrityNote.thinking-glance.label: Brief glance away
integrityNote.thinking-glance.explanatio: Ordinary. A short look away from the screen, which happens in every conversation and means nothing on its own. Shown so you can see it was noticed; it is never counted.
integrityNote.gaze-off-screen.label: Looked off-screen for a while
integrityNote.gaze-off-screen.explanatio: The head and eyes pointed away from the screen for several seconds. Looking away has many causes (recalling, planning an answer, nerves, reading something, a notification, a pet, a noise), and the camera cannot tell which; read it against the answer given. Low confidence: it comes from head direction, not from where the eyes were exactly.
integrityNote.reading-pattern.label: Reading pattern off-screen
integrityNote.reading-pattern.explanatio: Repeated sweeps and returns of the eyes toward one off-screen spot, the movement of reading text placed there. It can have other explanations; check it against the answers given. Evidence to weigh, never proof.
integrityNote.examiner-look-away.label: Looked away from the examiner while answering
integrityNote.examiner-look-away.explana: In the voice interview the student's head and eyes turned away from the examiner's face for a while during an answer (the summary says how long, and whether the examiner gave a short, gentle spoken reminder at a pause). Looking away has many causes (recalling, planning an answer, nerves, a noise, a habit, reading something), and the camera cannot tell which; read it against the answer. Low confidence: webcam gaze is good to a few degrees at best, never an exact point on the screen. The summary also gives the session's eye-tracking quality (good, fair or poor, and whether it was set up to the student's screen or used head direction only); weigh a fair or poor note even less.
integrityNote.examiner-reading.label: Reading-like eyes while answering
integrityNote.examiner-reading.explanati: During an answer the eyes swept and jumped back away from the examiner, which can be the movement of reading. Webcam eye tracking is too coarse to tell reading from other eye movement reliably, and the student may have been re-reading the question or transcript on screen; check it against the answer. Evidence to weigh, never proof.
integrityNote.examiner-face-absent.label: Face out of view while answering
integrityNote.examiner-face-absent.expla: The camera saw no face for part of an answer in the voice interview. Often harmless (leaning out of frame, the camera moved); check whether the answer continued.
integrityNote.examiner-second-face.label: Second face while answering
integrityNote.examiner-second-face.expla: The camera saw more than one face during an answer in the voice interview. It may be a person, a photo or a reflection; look at whether the answer changed around then.
integrityNote.examiner-fade.label: Screen dimmed for eye contact
integrityNote.examiner-fade.explanation: The exam screen faded, with a warning to look at the examiner, because the student looked away while answering; it cleared when they looked back. The summary gives how long and how far it faded. It records what the student saw, not a finding.
integrityNote.camera-unavailable.label: Camera not used
integrityNote.camera-unavailable.explana: Neutral. The camera checks did not run (the student did not allow the camera, there was no camera, or it could not be opened). The exam continued normally and nothing is inferred from it.
integrityNote.webcam-capped.label: More camera events not stored
integrityNote.webcam-capped.explanation: The camera checks kept reporting events past the per-session limit, so later ones were not stored. Usually poor lighting or framing making the face flicker in and out; look at the events that were stored.
integrityNote.second-speaker.label: A second voice
integrityNote.second-speaker.explanation: Another voice was heard during the answer. Could be coaching, or just someone else in the room; listen to the answer if audio is available.
integrityNote.whispering.label: Whispering heard
integrityNote.whispering.explanation: Quiet speech was heard that wasn't the answer itself. Some students murmur while thinking; weigh it with the answers around it.
integrityNote.reading-cadence.label: Reading-aloud rhythm
integrityNote.reading-cadence.explanatio: The answer's pace and pauses sounded like reading rather than talking. Weak evidence on its own; some people speak carefully when nervous.
integrityNote.fluent-after-silence.label: Long wait, then a smooth answer
integrityNote.fluent-after-silence.expla: A long gap before the first word, followed by an answer with none of the usual hesitation. Innocent explanations include planning the answer before speaking, or a student who simply speaks smoothly once ready. Weak evidence: weigh it against how the student answered other questions.
integrityNote.tab-hidden.label: Exam tab hidden
integrityNote.tab-hidden.explanation: The exam tab was hidden (another tab or window was in front). Could be looking something up, or a notification or accident; check the time it lasted.
integrityNote.focus-lost.label: Window lost focus
integrityNote.focus-lost.explanation: The exam window lost focus, usually a click on another window. Short blips are common and usually harmless.
integrityNote.fullscreen-exit.label: Left full screen
integrityNote.fullscreen-exit.explanatio: The student left full-screen mode. Often an accidental key press; look at what happened next.
integrityNote.extra-screen.label: Extra screen connected
integrityNote.extra-screen.explanation: The browser reported more than one screen. That alone is common (laptops on a monitor); it matters only with other signals.
integrityNote.paste.label: Pasted into the answer
integrityNote.paste.explanation: Text was pasted into the answer box rather than typed. Some students draft elsewhere or paste their own earlier words; compare the pasted answer with the student's other answers.
integrityNote.copy-question.label: Copied the question
integrityNote.copy-question.explanation: The question text was copied. Could be pasting it into a search or another tool, or just re-reading; check whether the tab was hidden or text pasted soon after.
integrityNote.devtools-open.label: Developer tools possibly open
integrityNote.devtools-open.explanation: A weak guess from the window's size: developer tools may have been open. Window zoom and browser side panels look the same; ignore it unless other signals line up.
integrityNote.signals-capped.label: More browser signals not stored
integrityNote.signals-capped.explanation: The browser kept reporting signals past the per-session limit, so later ones were not stored. Usually a flickering window or connection; look at the signals that were stored.
integrityNote.text-reads-as-written.expl: An unvalidated panel estimate that this answer reads more like text read aloud than the student's other answers. Estimates of this kind (detectors of machine-written text) misfire often, especially on non-native speakers, and this one's false-flag rate has not been measured. Context only: never a verdict, never a score, never meaningful on its own, and hidden from a blind grader until their grade is in.
integrityNote.possibly-recited.label: Possibly recited
integrityNote.possibly-recited.explanati: The recitation check found this answer closely follows the source material's wording, or was a long, fluent spoken answer that began only after a long silent wait (a read-out pattern; never applied to a student with extra time or on an exam that switched it off, since thinking before speaking looks the same); the turn shows the overlap, the copied stretch and which pattern fired. The examiner did not count it as evidence of the student's own understanding, either way, and asked them to say it differently, apply it, or explain why; read the next answer. Students quote and memorize honestly, so this is never a verdict of cheating.
integrityNote.window-away.label: Window away
integrityNote.window-away.explanation: A focus signal. Treat it as evidence to weigh with the answers around it, not as a finding.
